P7_direction_representativeness_limitati.cause: H1 bias was BEARISH for all 66 decision cycles in this DEVELOPMENT window (bias_counts.BEARISH=66, BULLISH=0 per SSC1D_WP2_BASELINE/wp2_baseline_report.json) -- SSC only trades in the direction of H1 bias, so a BEARISH-only window structurally produces SHORT-only occurrences.
P7_direction_representativeness_limitati.assessment: Every finding in this diagnosis (economic attribution, setup/session/SL/exit-capture patterns) describes SHORT-side behavior only. None of it can be generalized to LONG occurrences -- friction may differ by direction (asymmetric spread/slippage is possible but not evidenced either way here), and setup/session dynamics could plausibly differ for LONG entries for reasons this window cannot speak to (e.g. different session liquidity asymmetries). This is a genuine evidentiary gap, not a strategy defect.
P7_direction_representativeness_limitati.action_taken: No LONG trades were synthesized. The dataset was not broadened. This limitation is carried forward as a constraint on any future WP4 hypothesis scope, not resolved here.

P8_failure_mechanism_ranking.economic_contribution: friction_total_R = 5.886R, approximately equal in magnitude to the entire net loss (net_R = -5.877R), against a gross_expectancy_R of only +0.0003R
P8_failure_mechanism_ranking.supporting_metrics: 50.5% of all gross-positive R consumed by friction; friction fairly uniform across setups (0.151-0.238R mean) and sessions (0.173-0.208R mean) -- broad structural drag, not concentrated in one segment
P8_failure_mechanism_ranking.limitations: Exact arithmetic reconciliation (gross - friction = net, verified to 0.0 residual), not an inference -- the strongest-evidenced mechanism in this diagnosis by construction

P8_failure_mechanism_ranking.economic_contribution: SL-bucket net_R sums to roughly -13.47R (net_expectancy -1.224R x 11) versus SESSION_EXIT-bucket net_R of roughly +7.59R (net_expectancy +0.379R x 20) -- the SL bucket alone more than accounts for the total -5.877R net loss
P8_failure_mechanism_ranking.supporting_metrics: SL occurrences concentrate in ASIAN_LONDON (8/11) and cluster on 2 of 33 calendar days (5/11 SL occurrences on 2026-05-26 and 2026-06-01 alone); mean MAE -0.593R; only 4/11 reached MFE>=0.5R before stopping (a minority)
P8_failure_mechanism_ranking.limitations: Direct count/expectancy split already present in WP2's own decomposition, cross-validated here at occurrence level -- clustering on 2 days is suggestive but N=2 cluster-days is too small to claim a systematic calendar/event pattern

P8_failure_mechanism_ranking.economic_contribution: mean gap of 0.739R between MFE and realized gross_R across all 31 occurrences; not separable into a single R-figure of 'lost' economics without assuming a counterfactual exit rule, which this diagnosis does not do
P8_failure_mechanism_ranking.supporting_metrics: 12/31 occurrences (39%) show positive MFE with realized gross_R <= 0; mean MFE 0.739R vs mean realized gross_R 0.0003R
P8_failure_mechanism_ranking.limitations: Conflated across winning and losing occurrences and across exit reasons (session-exit trades that gave back gains vs SL trades with some prior favorable excursion are structurally different situations); this pilot's diagnosis contract (SSC1D_WP0_diagnosis_contract_schema.json) requires flagging that this exact mechanism -- exit-capture / target too far -- is ALREADY the subject of the OPEN canonical hypothesis HYP_001_EXIT_CAPTURE (artifacts/validation/ST_SESSION_SWEEP_CONTINUATION_V1/HYP_001_PREREGISTRATION/). Any future WP4 hypothesis touching this mechanism must explicitly acknowledge that overlap rather than treat it as a novel finding.
